newsitem.title: INDIA: India says no plans to build intermediate missile.
newsitem.headline: India says no plans to build intermediate missile.

text.p: India has successfully completed research on its intermediate-range Agni missile but does not plan to produce the weapon unless the nation's security is threatened, the defence ministry said on Thursday.

"Agni is a re-entry technology demonstration project which has been successfully completed and all the objectives have been met," the ministry said in a report to parliament. "Agni project did not envisage development of a missile system."

"The decision to develop and produce a missile system based on Agni technology, however, can be taken at an appropriate time consistent with the prevailing threat perception and global or regional security environment," a ministry spokesman said, reading from the report.
The report was presented to a standing committee in parliament in October and released on Thursday, the spokesman said.
India last tested the surface-to-surface Agni, designed to hit targets 2,500 km (1,500 miles) away and believed capable of carrying a nuclear warhead, in 1994.
The United States has urged New Delhi to halt missile testing permanently, fearing a major arms race between India and Pakistan, which have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947.
India detonated a nuclear device in 1974 but says it has not built a nuclear bomb. The United States believes both India and Pakistan could quickly assemble nuclear weapons.
The Agni, a 14-tonne, 19-metre (60-foot) rocket, was first tested successfully in May 1989, but failed to hit its target in the Bay of Bengal in a second test three years later.
A third attempt which failed was made in January 1994. The last launch, a success, came in February 1994.
India has insisted the Agni, named after the Hindu fire god, was not for military use but was being developed as part of an ambitious programme to launch its own satellites.
Washington had protested over the previous Agni tests, saying ballistic missile programmes undermine security in areas of regional tension.
